question.problem:
The area of a square with a side length of $9\,\text{cm}$ is{{field-1}}
${\text{cm}}^{2}.$

current_example.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144298/assets/7e300a90dbfda5a9210cec502c2879b7950e2765c433eb6ee6284e74db3cd220.png)

 What is the area of the square above?
current_example.worked_solution:
To calculate the area $A$ of a square, we square its side length. Therefore, the area of the square is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =(5\,\text{ft})^{2} \\  & =5\,\text{ft}\times 5\,\text{ft} \\  & =(5\times 5)\times (\text{ft}\times \text{ft}) \\  & =25\,{\text{ft}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
